4//! Rendering strips.
5
6use crate::third_party::vello_common::flatten::Line;
7use crate::third_party::vello_common::peniko::Fill;
8use crate::third_party::vello_common::tile::{Tile, Tiles};
9use crate::third_party::vello_common::util::f32_to_u8;
10use alloc::vec::Vec;
11use fearless_simd::*;
12
13/// A strip.
14#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
15pub struct Strip {
16    /// The x coordinate of the strip, in user coordinates.
17    pub x: u16,
18    /// The y coordinate of the strip, in user coordinates.
19    pub y: u16,
20    /// Packed alpha index and fill gap flag.
21    ///
22    /// Bit layout (u32):
23    /// - bit 31: `fill_gap` (See `Strip::fill_gap()`).
24    /// - bits 0..=30: `alpha_idx` (See `Strip::alpha_idx()`).
25    packed_alpha_idx_fill_gap: u32,
26}
27
28impl Strip {
29    /// The bit mask for `fill_gap` packed into `packed_alpha_idx_fill_gap`.
30    const FILL_GAP_MASK: u32 = 1 << 31;
31
32    /// Creates a new strip.
33    pub fn new(x: u16, y: u16, alpha_idx: u32, fill_gap: bool) -> Self {
34        // Ensure `alpha_idx` does not collide with the fill flag bit.
35        assert!(alpha_idx & Self::FILL_GAP_MASK == 0, "`alpha_idx` too large");
36        let fill_gap = u32::from(fill_gap) << 31;
37        Self { x, y, packed_alpha_idx_fill_gap: alpha_idx | fill_gap }
38    }
39
40    /// Return whether the strip is a sentinel strip.
41    pub fn is_sentinel(&self) -> bool {
42        self.x == u16::MAX
43    }
44
45    /// Return the y coordinate of the strip, in strip units.
46    pub fn strip_y(&self) -> u16 {
47        self.y / Tile::HEIGHT
48    }
49
50    /// Returns the alpha index.
51    #[inline(always)]
52    pub fn alpha_idx(&self) -> u32 {
53        self.packed_alpha_idx_fill_gap & !Self::FILL_GAP_MASK
54    }
55
56    /// Sets the alpha index.
57    ///
58    /// Note that the largest value that can be stored in the alpha index is `u32::MAX << 1`, as the
59    /// highest bit is reserved for `fill_gap`.
60    #[inline(always)]
61    pub fn set_alpha_idx(&mut self, alpha_idx: u32) {
62        // Ensure `alpha_idx` does not collide with the fill flag bit.
63        assert!(alpha_idx & Self::FILL_GAP_MASK == 0, "`alpha_idx` too large");
64        let fill_gap = self.packed_alpha_idx_fill_gap & Self::FILL_GAP_MASK;
65        self.packed_alpha_idx_fill_gap = alpha_idx | fill_gap;
66    }
67
68    /// Returns whether the gap that lies between this strip and the previous in the same row should be filled.
69    #[inline(always)]
70    pub fn fill_gap(&self) -> bool {
71        (self.packed_alpha_idx_fill_gap & Self::FILL_GAP_MASK) != 0
72    }
73
74    /// Sets whether the gap that lies between this strip and the previous in the same row should be filled.
75    #[inline(always)]
76    pub fn set_fill_gap(&mut self, fill: bool) {
77        let fill = u32::from(fill) << 31;
78        self.packed_alpha_idx_fill_gap = (self.packed_alpha_idx_fill_gap & !Self::FILL_GAP_MASK) | fill;
79    }
80
81    /// When early culling is active, geometry fully to the left of the viewport creates no tiles.
82    /// However, if that geometry has a non-zero winding (e.g. a large shape surrounding the
83    /// viewport), then we must output strips for those fills.
84    ///
85    /// We reconstruct this "background" fill using `row_windings` (the winding at x=0) to emit solid
86    /// strips for:
87    ///      1. All rows vertically above the first visible tile.
88    ///      2. 'Captive' rows between two tile-containing rows.
89    ///      3. All rows vertically below the last visible tile.
90    #[inline(always)]
91    fn emit_culled_background<F>(
92        start: u16,
93        end: u16,
94        strips: &mut Vec<Self>,
95        alphas: &mut Vec<u8>,
96        windings: &crate::third_party::vello_common::tile::CulledWindings,
97        mut should_fill: F,
98    ) where
99        F: FnMut(i32) -> bool,
100    {
101        windings.for_active_rows_in_range(start as usize, end as usize, |row| {
102            if should_fill(windings.coarse[row] as i32) {
103                let y_pos = row as u16 * Tile::HEIGHT;
104                strips.push(Self::new(0, y_pos, alphas.len() as u32, false));
105                alphas.extend([255_u8; Tile::HEIGHT as usize * Tile::WIDTH as usize]);
106                // TODO: Clamp to the scene width instead of u16::MAX; in the future there might
107                // not be clamping on the x.
108                strips.push(Self::new(u16::MAX, y_pos, alphas.len() as u32, true));
109            }
110        });
111    }
112}
113
114/// Render the tiles stored in `tiles` into the strip and alpha buffer.
115pub fn render(
116    level: Level,
117    tiles: &Tiles,
118    strip_buf: &mut Vec<Strip>,
119    alpha_buf: &mut Vec<u8>,
120    fill_rule: Fill,
121    aliasing_threshold: Option<u8>,
122    lines: &[Line],
123) {
124    dispatch!(level, simd => render_impl(simd,
125                                         tiles,
126                                         strip_buf,
127                                         alpha_buf,
128                                         fill_rule,
129                                         aliasing_threshold,
130                                         lines));
131}
132
133#[inline(always)]
134fn render_impl<S: Simd>(
135    s: S,
136    tiles: &Tiles,
137    strip_buf: &mut Vec<Strip>,
138    alpha_buf: &mut Vec<u8>,
139    fill_rule: Fill,
140    aliasing_threshold: Option<u8>,
141    lines: &[Line],
142) {
143    let row_windings = &tiles.windings.coarse;
144    let has_culled_tiles = tiles.has_culled_tiles();
145
146    // If no tiles were culled and the tile buffer is empty, we can simply exit. If tiles were
147    // culled, the tile buffer may be empty but there may be winding produced by culled geometry
148    // left of the viewport that must be checked for filling.
149    if !has_culled_tiles && tiles.is_empty() {
150        return;
151    }
152
153    let should_fill = |winding: i32| match fill_rule {
154        Fill::NonZero => winding != 0,
155        Fill::EvenOdd => winding % 2 != 0,
156    };
157
158    // Helper to handle "captive strips". When a row has tiles, but the first tile
159    // is not at the left edge of the viewport (x != 0), we must emit a solid strip
160    // from x=0 to that tile if the coarse winding dictates a fill.
161    let emit_captive_strip = |y: u16, is_left_viewport: bool, strips: &mut Vec<Strip>, alphas: &mut Vec<u8>| {
162        let coarse_wd = tiles.windings.coarse[y as usize] as i32;
163
164        if should_fill(coarse_wd) && !is_left_viewport {
165            strips.push(Strip::new(0, y * Tile::HEIGHT, alphas.len() as u32, false));
166            alphas.extend([255_u8; Tile::HEIGHT as usize * Tile::WIDTH as usize]);
167        }
168
169        let mut acc = f32x4::splat(s, coarse_wd as f32);
170        if is_left_viewport {
171            let fine_winding: f32x4<_> = tiles.windings.partial[y as usize].simd_into(s);
172            acc += fine_winding;
173        }
174
175        (coarse_wd, acc)
176    };
177
178    // The accumulated tile winding delta. A line that crosses the top edge of a tile
179    // increments the delta if the line is directed upwards, and decrements it if goes
180    // downwards. Horizontal lines leave it unchanged.
181    let mut winding_delta: i32 = 0;
182
183    // The previous tile visited.
184    let mut prev_tile = if has_culled_tiles && tiles.is_empty() { Tile::SENTINEL } else { *tiles.get(0) };
185
186    // The accumulated (fractional) winding of the tile-sized location we're currently at.
187    // Note multiple tiles can be at the same location.
188    // Note that we are also implicitly assuming here that the tile height exactly fits into a
189    // SIMD vector (i.e. 128 bits).
190    let mut location_winding = [f32x4::splat(s, 0.0); Tile::WIDTH as usize];
191    // The accumulated (fractional) windings at this location's right edge. When we move to the
192    // next location, this is splatted to that location's starting winding.
193    let mut accumulated_winding = f32x4::splat(s, 0.0);
194
195    let left_viewport = prev_tile.x == 0;
196    if has_culled_tiles {
197        let row_max = prev_tile.y.min(row_windings.len() as u16);
198        Strip::emit_culled_background(0, row_max, strip_buf, alpha_buf, &tiles.windings, should_fill);
199        if tiles.is_empty() {
200            return;
201        }
202        let (wd, acc) = emit_captive_strip(prev_tile.y, left_viewport, strip_buf, alpha_buf);
203        winding_delta = wd;
204        accumulated_winding = acc;
205        location_winding = [accumulated_winding; Tile::WIDTH as usize];
206    }
207
208    // The strip we're building.
209    let mut strip =
210        Strip::new(prev_tile.x * Tile::WIDTH, prev_tile.y * Tile::HEIGHT, alpha_buf.len() as u32, should_fill(winding_delta) && !left_viewport);
211
212    for (tile_idx, tile) in tiles.iter().copied().chain([Tile::SENTINEL]).enumerate() {
213        let line = lines[tile.line_idx() as usize];
214        let tile_left_x = f32::from(tile.x) * f32::from(Tile::WIDTH);
215        let tile_top_y = f32::from(tile.y) * f32::from(Tile::HEIGHT);
216        let p0_x = line.p0.x - tile_left_x;
217        let p0_y = line.p0.y - tile_top_y;
218        let p1_x = line.p1.x - tile_left_x;
219        let p1_y = line.p1.y - tile_top_y;
220
221        // Push out the winding as an alpha mask when we move to the next location (i.e., a tile
222        // without the same location).
223        if !prev_tile.same_loc(&tile) {
224            match fill_rule {
225                Fill::NonZero => {
226                    let p1 = f32x4::splat(s, 0.5);
227                    let p2 = f32x4::splat(s, 255.0);
228
229                    #[expect(clippy::needless_range_loop, reason = "dimension clarity")]
230                    for x in 0..Tile::WIDTH as usize {
231                        let area = location_winding[x];
232                        let coverage = area.abs();
233                        let mulled = coverage.mul_add(p2, p1);
234                        // Note that we are not storing the location winding here but the actual
235                        // alpha value as f32, so we reuse the variable as a temporary storage.
236                        // Also note that we need the `min` here because the winding can be > 1
237                        // and thus the calculated alpha value need to be clamped to 255.
238                        location_winding[x] = mulled.min(p2);
239                    }
240                }
241                Fill::EvenOdd => {
242                    let p1 = f32x4::splat(s, 0.5);
243                    let p2 = f32x4::splat(s, -2.0);
244                    let p3 = f32x4::splat(s, 255.0);
245
246                    #[expect(clippy::needless_range_loop, reason = "dimension clarity")]
247                    for x in 0..Tile::WIDTH as usize {
248                        let area = location_winding[x];
249                        let im1 = area.mul_add(p1, p1).floor();
250                        let coverage = p2.mul_add(im1, area).abs();
251                        let mulled = p3.mul_add(coverage, p1);
252                        // TODO: It is possible that, unlike for `NonZero`, we don't need the `min`
253                        // here.
254                        location_winding[x] = mulled.min(p3);
255                    }
256                }
257            };
258
259            let p1 = s.combine_f32x4(location_winding[0], location_winding[1]);
260            let p2 = s.combine_f32x4(location_winding[2], location_winding[3]);
261
262            let mut u8_vals = f32_to_u8(s.combine_f32x8(p1, p2));
263
264            if let Some(aliasing_threshold) = aliasing_threshold {
265                u8_vals = s.select_u8x16(u8_vals.simd_ge(u8x16::splat(s, aliasing_threshold)), u8x16::splat(s, 255), u8x16::splat(s, 0));
266            }
267
268            alpha_buf.extend_from_slice(u8_vals.as_slice());
269
270            #[expect(clippy::needless_range_loop, reason = "dimension clarity")]
271            for x in 0..Tile::WIDTH as usize {
272                location_winding[x] = accumulated_winding;
273            }
274        }
275
276        // Push out the strip if we're moving to a next strip.
277        if !prev_tile.same_loc(&tile) && !prev_tile.prev_loc(&tile) {
278            debug_assert_eq!(
279                (prev_tile.x as u32 + 1) * Tile::WIDTH as u32 - strip.x as u32,
280                ((alpha_buf.len() - strip.alpha_idx() as usize) / usize::from(Tile::HEIGHT)) as u32,
281                "The number of columns written to the alpha buffer should equal the number of columns spanned by this strip."
282            );
283            strip_buf.push(strip);
284
285            let is_sentinel = tile_idx == tiles.len() as usize;
286            let left_viewport = tile.x == 0;
287            if !prev_tile.same_row(&tile) {
288                // Emit a final strip in the row if there is non-zero winding for the sparse fill,
289                // or unconditionally if we've reached the sentinel tile to end the path (the
290                // `alpha_idx` field is used for width calculations).
291                if winding_delta != 0 || is_sentinel {
292                    strip_buf.push(Strip::new(u16::MAX, prev_tile.y * Tile::HEIGHT, alpha_buf.len() as u32, should_fill(winding_delta)));
293                }
294
295                // Logic identical to the start (see above): fill any vertical gaps (empty rows)
296                // between the previous and current tile using the row windings.
297                if has_culled_tiles && !is_sentinel {
298                    Strip::emit_culled_background(prev_tile.y + 1, tile.y, strip_buf, alpha_buf, &tiles.windings, should_fill);
299
300                    let (wd, acc) = emit_captive_strip(tile.y, left_viewport, strip_buf, alpha_buf);
301                    winding_delta = wd;
302                    accumulated_winding = acc;
303                } else {
304                    winding_delta = 0;
305                    accumulated_winding = f32x4::splat(s, 0.0);
306                };
307
308                #[expect(clippy::needless_range_loop, reason = "dimension clarity")]
309                for x in 0..Tile::WIDTH as usize {
310                    location_winding[x] = accumulated_winding;
311                }
312            } else {
313                // Note: this fill is mathematically not necessary. It provides a way to reduce
314                // accumulation of float rounding errors.
315                accumulated_winding = f32x4::splat(s, winding_delta as f32);
316            }
317
318            if is_sentinel {
319                break;
320            }
321
322            strip = Strip::new(tile.x * Tile::WIDTH, tile.y * Tile::HEIGHT, alpha_buf.len() as u32, should_fill(winding_delta) && !left_viewport);
323        }
324        prev_tile = tile;
325
326        // TODO: horizontal geometry has no impact on winding. This branch will be removed when
327        // horizontal geometry is culled at the tile-generation stage.
328        if p0_y == p1_y {
329            continue;
330        }
331
332        // Lines moving upwards (in a y-down coordinate system) add to winding; lines moving
333        // downwards subtract from winding.
334        let sign = (p0_y - p1_y).signum();
335
336        // Calculate winding / pixel area coverage.
337        //
338        // Conceptually, horizontal rays are shot from left to right. Every time the ray crosses a
339        // line that is directed upwards (decreasing `y`), the winding is incremented. Every time
340        // the ray crosses a line moving downwards (increasing `y`), the winding is decremented.
341        // The fractional area coverage of a pixel is the integral of the winding within it.
342        //
343        // Practically, to calculate this, each pixel is considered individually, and we determine
344        // whether the line moves through this pixel. The line's y-delta within this pixel is
345        // accumulated and added to the area coverage of pixels to the right. Within the pixel
346        // itself, the area to the right of the line segment forms a trapezoid (or a triangle in
347        // the degenerate case). The area of this trapezoid is added to the pixel's area coverage.
348        //
349        // For example, consider the following pixel square, with a line indicated by asterisks
350        // starting inside the pixel and crossing its bottom edge. The area covered is the
351        // trapezoid on the bottom-right enclosed by the line and the pixel square. The area is
352        // positive if the line moves down, and negative otherwise.
353        //
354        //  __________________
355        //  |                |
356        //  |         *------|
357        //  |        *       |
358        //  |       *        |
359        //  |      *         |
360        //  |     *          |
361        //  |    *           |
362        //  |___*____________|
363        //     *
364        //    *
365
366        let (line_top_y, line_top_x, line_bottom_y, line_bottom_x) = if p0_y < p1_y { (p0_y, p0_x, p1_y, p1_x) } else { (p1_y, p1_x, p0_y, p0_x) };
367
368        let y_slope = (line_bottom_y - line_top_y) / (line_bottom_x - line_top_x);
369        let x_slope = 1. / y_slope;
370
371        winding_delta += sign as i32 * i32::from(tile.winding());
372
373        let line_top_y = f32x4::splat(s, line_top_y);
374        let line_bottom_y = f32x4::splat(s, line_bottom_y);
375
376        // See the explanation of this term on the `line_px_left_yx` and `line_px_right_yx`
377        // variables below.
378        let line_px_base_yx = line_top_y.mul_add(-x_slope, line_top_x);
379
380        let px_top_y = f32x4::simd_from(s, [0., 1., 2., 3.]);
381        let px_bottom_y = 1. + px_top_y;
382
383        let ymin = line_top_y.max(px_top_y);
384        let ymax = line_bottom_y.min(px_bottom_y);
385
386        let mut acc = f32x4::splat(s, 0.0);
387
388        for x_idx in 0..Tile::WIDTH {
389            let x_idx_s = f32x4::splat(s, x_idx as f32);
390            let px_left_x = x_idx_s;
391            let px_right_x = 1.0 + x_idx_s;
392
393            // The y-coordinate of the intersections between the line and the pixel's left and
394            // right edges respectively.
395            //
396            // There is some subtlety going on here: `y_slope` will usually be finite, but will
397            // be `inf` for purely vertical lines (`p0_x == p1_x`).
398            //
399            // In the case of `inf`, the resulting slope calculation will be `-inf` or `inf`
400            // depending on whether the pixel edge is left or right of the line, respectively
401            // (from the viewport's coordinate system perspective). The `min` and `max`
402            // y-clamping logic generalizes nicely, as a pixel edge to the left of the line is
403            // clamped to `ymin`, and a pixel edge to the right is clamped to `ymax`.
404            //
405            // In the special case where a vertical line and pixel edge are at the exact same
406            // x-position (collinear), the line belongs to the pixel on whose _left_ edge it is
407            // situated. The resulting slope calculation for the edge the line is situated on
408            // will be NaN, as `0 * inf` results in NaN. This is true for both the left and
409            // right edge.
410            //
411            // We know `ymin` and `ymax` are finite. We require the `max` operation to pick `ymin`
412            // if its first operand is NaN. On x86, that maps to the semantics of `_mm_max_ps`,
413            // which `f32x4::max` emits: that instruction takes element-wise
414            // `if first > second { first } else { second }`. For AArch64, we do require the
415            // `f32x4::max_precise` semantics (as `vmax_f32` returns NaN if either operand is NaN);
416            // however, for AArch64 the precise version should be comparatively less expensive than
417            // on x86. For `min`, we then know both operands are finite, so we can unambiguously
418            // use the relaxed version. If this ever breaks, tests should fail loudly, because NaNs
419            // happen a lot here!
420            trait F32x4MaxExt {
421                fn max_if_first_nan_take_second(self, rhs: Self) -> Self;
422            }
423            #[cfg(any(target_arch = "x86", target_arch = "x86_64"))]
424            impl<S: Simd> F32x4MaxExt for f32x4<S> {
425                #[inline(always)]
426                fn max_if_first_nan_take_second(self, rhs: Self) -> Self {
427                    self.max(rhs)
428                }
429            }
430            #[cfg(not(any(target_arch = "x86", target_arch = "x86_64")))]
431            impl<S: Simd> F32x4MaxExt for f32x4<S> {
432                #[inline(always)]
433                fn max_if_first_nan_take_second(self, rhs: Self) -> Self {
434                    self.max_precise(rhs)
435                }
436            }
437            let line_px_left_y = (px_left_x - line_top_x).mul_add(y_slope, line_top_y).max_if_first_nan_take_second(ymin).min(ymax);
438            let line_px_right_y = (px_right_x - line_top_x).mul_add(y_slope, line_top_y).max_if_first_nan_take_second(ymin).min(ymax);
439
440            // For each pixel we calculate the x-coordinates of the left- and rightmost points on
441            // the line segment within that pixel. We do this based on the y-offsets of those two
442            // points from the top of the line. This can be calculated as, e.g.,
443            // `(line_px_left_y - line_top_y) * x_slope + line_top_x`.
444            //
445            // Rather than calculating that y-offset twice for each pixel within the loop through
446            // subtracting from the points' y-coordinates, we get rid of that subtraction by baking
447            // it into the algebraic "base" x-coordinate `line_px_base_yx` calculated above the
448            // loop. When adding that term to `y * x_slope` it gives the x-coordinate of the point
449            // along the line.
450            //
451            // Note `x_slope` is always finite, as horizontal geometry is elided.
452            let line_px_left_yx = line_px_left_y.mul_add(x_slope, line_px_base_yx);
453            let line_px_right_yx = line_px_right_y.mul_add(x_slope, line_px_base_yx);
454            let h = (line_px_right_y - line_px_left_y).abs();
455
456            // The trapezoidal area enclosed between the line and the right edge of the pixel
457            // square. More straightforwardly written as follows, but the `madd` is faster.
458            // 0.5 * h * (2. * px_right_x - line_px_right_yx - line_px_left_yx).
459            let area = h * (line_px_right_yx + line_px_left_yx).mul_add(-0.5, px_right_x);
460            location_winding[x_idx as usize] += area.mul_add(sign, acc);
461            acc = h.mul_add(sign, acc);
462        }
463
464        accumulated_winding += acc;
465    }
466
467    if has_culled_tiles {
468        Strip::emit_culled_background(
469            (prev_tile.y + 1).min(row_windings.len() as u16),
470            row_windings.len() as u16,
471            strip_buf,
472            alpha_buf,
473            &tiles.windings,
474            should_fill,
475        );
476    }
477}
